1.

Mistweaver Monk Overview

The Mistweaver specialization is versatile, and different talent choices can allow it to fit a wide range of raid requirements. Mistweavers can, therefore, heal both tanks and the raid very well.

Based on talent choices, Mistweavers can be either unparalleled tank healers with strong area of effect throughput or damage-dealing mobile raid healers.

Requires some tuning Mistweaver Monk is a throughput healer, and as such, lives and dies by its ability to top up health bars. Unlike other specs that bring powerful mitigation or utility spells to bypass certain mechanics, Mistweaver relies solely on its HPS throughput. Unfortunately, 12.1 saw several aura nerfs to Mistweaver's throughput, as well as sizable buffs almost every other healer spec, making our niche in raid somewhat dubious at the time of writing.
Middle of the pack Mistweaver Monk is a strong option in Mythic+, in no small part due to our immense durability. Mistweavers have a plethora of damage reduction cooldowns and passives that allow us to take a substantial amount of punishment without dying. Furthermore, Mistweaver's kit is designed around dealing damage, passively increasing your group's total DPS. However, where Mistweaver falls short is its lack of meaningful group utility; we do not bring a strong group-wide damage reduction like Spirit Link Totem or Power Word: Barrier, nor do we have a battle resurrection or Bloodlust. Equally, our external DR cooldown Life Cocoon provides a flat amount of damage prevention, meaning it scales less effectively into higher keys than other healer's cooldowns like Ironbark or Pain Suppression. All that being said though, while a Mistweaver likely won't be used in a rank 1 run, they absolutely still excel in bleeding edge keys.
Niche Utility Utility is Mistweaver Monk's Achilles' heel; while we do have numerous interesting utility options, many of them are particularly niche during combat. The obvious stand-outs for us are Ring of Peace, Leg Sweep, and Paralysis which give us excellent group CC ability in dungeons, however it is extremely rare that a strategy will uniquely revolve around any of those abilities in specific; other classes can be brought to do the same thing. Our raid cooldown Revival includes a group-wide magic dispel, but given the current design philosophy of debuffs often requiring intentionally timed dispels, this effect is often a detriment rather than a boon (so much so that Revival as a talent exists on a choice node with another talent Restoral, which does the exact same thing, just with no dispel). Lastly, we bring the debuff Mystic Touch as a monk specific raid buff. However, the debuff can also be brought by a Windwalker or Brewmaster, and as far buffs go, 5% physical damage is among the weaker buffs as most damage in WoW is magical.
Extremely Durable Mistweaver Monk is one of the most durable specs in the game. With talents like Dance of the Wind making us straight up immune to certain attacks, as well a personal DR cooldown Fortifying Brew, and a plethora of passive damage reduction talents, it is very hard for a Mistweaver to run out of defensive options.
Hyper Mobile In terms of mobility few specs can hold a candle to a Monk's toolkit. Between Roll, Tiger's Lust, Transcendence, and Lighter Than Air, it is almost impossible to be caught flat-footed as a Mistweaver.
Strong Damage Mistweaver is largely designed around dealing damage to a target in order to heal, either directly through effects like Ancient Teachings or by buffing our spells like Rising Mist and Rushing Wind Kick. As such, Mistweavers will passively do more damage than the average healer, however with proper play, certain healers can exceed our top end throughput.

2.3.

Class Changes

Prior to the release of Season 2, Mistweaver (among other specs) has received a much welcome tuning pass. The buffs we received are substantial, but it is still unclear if they will make up for the deficit we saw during PTR testing.

/
Pre-Season Tuning
  • All healing increased by 8%. Does not affect PvP combat.
  • Venomous Abyss 4-set bonus has been updated – Activation rate increased by 33%.
2.3.1.

Patch 12.1 Launch Changes

This is a tough patch for Mistweaver. This patch cycle saw us receive a 3% and an 8% aura nerf to all our healing, as well as a re-tuning of our DPS-to-Healing mechanics. There seems to be an attempt to make Mastery a valuable stat again, however the new interactions of a high mastery build + our set bonus were cut down with a 60% nerf to Morning Breeze.

It remains to be seen just how these changes will truly affect Mistweaver once the Raid releases, but currently available data from PTR paints a troubling picture.

In Mythic+ Mistweaver remains decent, though our over reliance on Spinning Crane Kick has been tamped down through a series of nerfs and bug fixes. While you will still press SCK during larger AoE pulls, anything under five mobs will have us returning to Tiger Palm and Blackout Kick.

12.1 Class Tuning
  • New Talent: Vital Expenditure — Soothing Mist’s healing is increased by 300%, but its mana cost is increased by 200%. Choice node with Dancing Mists.
  • All healing reduced by ~10.7%.
  • Mastery: Gust of Mist healing increased by 225%.
  • Spinning Crane Kick damage decreased by 6.5%.
  • Way of the Crane now transfers 280% of damage done (was 340%).
  • Jadefire Teachings now increases Ancient Teaching’s transfer amount by 320% (was 270%).
  • Resolved an issue that caused Temple Training’s Spinning Crane Kick damage increase to apply to Mistweaver.
  • Morning Breeze effectiveness reduced by 60%.

2.4.

Patch 12.0.5 changes for Mistweaver Monk

This patch sees some tuning changes to our throughput to tamp down how powerful Mistweaver is in raid, while also adding some nice quality of life changes to our Apex and Hero talents. The main change here is a 5% HPS reduction to all our casted heals. It should be noted that this does not affect our damage transfer healing, so raiders will be more acutely affected than Mythic+ players.

While 5% is a significant nerf, as of the time of writing, Mistweaver, Discipline Priest, and Preservation Evoker are all massively out performing the rest of the other healing specs, and as such, each of them are having their numbers tuned down.

Ultimately, though this patch will aim to make the under performing healers more competitive, Mistweaver will still retain its spot as one of the highest throughput healers in raid.

12.0.5 Class Tuning
  • All healing reduced by 5%.
  • Sheilun's Gift healing is increased by 5% per cloud consumed (was 10%).
  • Spiritfont now causes Enveloping Mist to be instant cast.
  • Way of the Serpent no longer causes Soothing Mist and Crackling Jade Lightning to be cast while moving. This is now default behavior.
  • Conduit of the Celestials:
    • Inner Compass now rotates its stances on an 8 second timer.
  • Master of Harmony:
    • Harmonic Surge has been redesigned — Casting Thunder Focus Tea grants 2 charges of Potential Energy. Your next cast of Tiger Palm or Vivify consumes all charges of Potential Energy to cause a Harmonic Surge. Harmonic Surge: For each charge of Potential Energy, deal Nature damage to your target and nearby enemies, and heal up to 5 allies. Damage and healing increased per stack of Potential Energy consumed.
    • Potential Energy has been redesigned — Casting Rising Sun Kick or Rushing Wind Kick grants a charge of Potential Energy.
    • Coalescence's tooltip has been adjusted for clarity, and it now applies its own distinct periodic healing and damage effect.
2.5.

Midnight Season 1 Changes

With the release of Midnight's first season, like with most classes, Mistweaver received some tuning. These changes are mostly positive and primarily effect our Mythic+ gameplay through increases to Jadefire Teachings and changes to the healing profiles of Sheilun's Gift and Way of the Crane.

The baseline strength of Sheilun's gift is now higher with its strength becoming weaker at four clouds and beyond. This makes spamming it in high damage single target situations much more attractive, while toning down the max strength of a fully stacked SG. Similarly, Way of the Crane received a slight reduction in total HPS transfer, however it now funnels its healing into a single target, making the talent much more effective at healing tanks during large pulls, and about the same at healing group AoE.

Midnight Class Tuning
  • Sheilun's Gift healing increased by 60%
  • Sheilun's Gift clouds now increase its healing by 10% per stack (was 33%)
  • Jadefire Teachings now increases the transfer rate of Ancient Teachings by 260% (was 200%)
  • Way of the Crane now transfers 340% of damage onto 1 ally (was 125% onto 3 allies)
  • Jadefire Stomp damage now transfers into Ancient Teachings at 20% effectiveness
  • Invigorating Mists healing increased by 30%
2.6.

Midnight for Mistweaver Monk

Mistweaver received a myriad of changes in Midnight, largely aimed at reducing the amount of buffs and passive interactions that needed to be maintained in order to succeed. The spec plays fairly similarly to how it has in the past, albeit somewhat simplified.

Broadly speaking, the tempo of healing in general has slowed down quite a bit. Power has been taken out of our cooldowns and, for Mistweavers in specific, many of our healing amplifiers have been nerfed or removed entirely. The core theme and loop of our spec remains unchanged though: we're still a melee-dps healer who wants to blanket their group in Renewing Mist.

2.7.

Apex Talents

Midnight has expanded on the Talent system by introducing Apex Talents; effectively a powerful ability at the end of the class tree that players can opt into starting at level 81. For Mistweavers, that ability is Spiritfont. You will be able to allocate up to 4 talents points to increase your Apex Talent's power:

  1. Spiritfont — Causes your Vivify and Rising Sun Kick to grant you a buff that causes your next Enveloping Mist to channel Soothing Mist onto up to 5 targets at 20% effectiveness. If a target is at max Health, the Soothing Mist will jump to a new target, or split its healing among the other 4 targets.
  2. Spiritfont — Rising Sun Kick damage is increased by 10%/20% and Enveloping Mist healing is increased by 10%/20%. This bonus is increased by 50% while Spirit Font is active.
  3. Spiritfont — Thunder Focus Tea activates Spirit Font, and applies Chi Cocoons to targeted allies at 30% effectiveness.
2.8.

Hero Talent Changes

Conduit of the Celestials is largely the same, save for a few changed talents. Chi-Ji's Swiftness was moved and in its place we received Stampede of the Ancients which increases the healing of your Strength of the Black Ox shield by 400%. Additionally, since Refreshing Jade Wind was removed, the talents that affected it have been reworked to provide small passive bonuses to damage/healing.

Master of Harmony functions very similarly, but did get a fairly impactful rework to the function of the caption talent Coalescence. Now, the healing intensification is capped at 20% additional healing, instead fully withdrawing your banked vitality. Additionally, Vivify / Sheilun's Gift no longer generate vitality and instead will always withdraw vitality, increasing their healing by up to 100%.

2.9.

Rotational Changes

Moment to moment gameplay has changed very little, but minutia of the spec has been simplified. We still want to achieve a high uptime and spread of Renewing Mist as well as look to set up frequent Invoke Yu'lon, the Jade Serpent windows. Mana is more sparse even though the raw mana return from Mana Tea was buffed, it no longer reduces the mana cost of your spells.

2.10.

Utility Changes

Midnight has brought a massive reduction in defensiveness across the board, and Mistweaver is no exception. Diffuse Magic was reworked and now instead of being a damage reduction cooldown, instead causes Fortifying Brew to dispel a magic effect on you. Bounce Back was also removed, which accounted for a substantial amount of our durability. That being said, we are still one of the tankiest healers in the game; we retained most of our damage reduction talents and gained a few bonuses to the amount of healing we receive.

3.

Basics of Mistweaver Monk Gameplay

Like all healers, a Mistweaver needs to have a solid understanding of their spells so that they know which one to use in any given context. Unlike DPS, who can follow a rotation or priority queue, Healers are much more contextual.

Your aim needs to be maximizing efficient casts to squeeze the most healing out of your Mana bar. A high uptime and coverage of Renewing Mist is ideal is almost every situation for a Mistweaver as it is the driver for an enormous swath of our healing. You should be looking to use your cooldowns such as Invoke Yu'lon, the Jade Serpent, Invoke Chi-Ji, the Red Crane and Revival as frequently as the fight allows, as these large cooldowns generally result in the strongest throughput (and by proxy mana efficiency) that our kit has to offer. Lastly, to keep up with your mana consumption, you should be mindful to use Mana Tea enough as to not overcap your stacks.

The backbone of Mistweaver Monk can be condensed into the following ideas.

  • Renewing Mist is Life
    An enormous swath of Mistweaver's kit revolves around Renewing Mist. It's a powerful HoT all on its own, and it enables your bread and butter Vivify to hit additional targets. Make sure to cast this ability as close to on cooldown as possible to ensure proper coverage on your group.
  • You are a Melee Class
    While Mistweaver can cast and do the majority of its rotation from ranged, in terms of targeting for boss mechanics, the game will treat you as melee. It's important to take advantage of that to leave room for your ranged players. Ability targeting is more nuanced than that, but generally you will be immune to ranged only mechanics unless they specifically target healers.
  • Don't Forget Mana Tea!
    Mistweavers have active mana regeneration: spending mana generates Mana Tea stacks and consuming Mana Tea stacks generates mana. However Mana Tea only stacks up to 20 and it is easy to forget to use Mana Tea if you aren't low on mana! Ensuring that you're using Mana Tea before you cap will ensure you don't run OOM later on.
